target.title: chore: resolve gollaw code health audit findings (#293)
target.body:
## Summary

Systematic code-health and hardening pass for wacli using a stricter local build of
gollaw, plus targeted refactors in wacli where the findings represented real
maintainability, API-surface, duplication, dead-code, or security risk.

This PR now brings wacli to a clean default gollaw gate:

| Scan | main | This branch |
|------|------|-------------|
| Default gollaw | 24 findings: 1 critical, 23 warning | 0 findings |
| Strict hint scan | 113 findings: 1 critical, 23 warning, 4 info, 85 hint | 2 info only |

The two remaining strict-mode findings are informational build-tag notices:

- `internal/lock/lock_unix.go`: guarded by `!windows`
- `internal/syscontacts/other.go`: guarded by `!darwin`

Those are intentional OS-specific files, not code-health issues to remove.

Refs #293.

## Confirmed issues solved

- Removed the critical SQL-construction finding present on `main`.
- Reduced the default Gollaw gate from `24` findings on `main` to `0` findings on this branch.
- Reduced the strict hint scan from `113` findings on `main` to `2` informational build-tag notices.
- Removed critical/warning/hint-level Gollaw findings without `//gollaw:keep`, ignores, or relaxed yaml policy.
- Broke up large Cobra command constructors and command `RunE` bodies into focused option structs and `run*` helpers.
- Reduced duplicated send/select/status/sticker/file command plumbing.
- Extracted repeated sync, backfill, message-store, poll, status, media, and WA client logic into smaller helpers.
- Tightened unexported/internal types and helper names where they were only used inside one package.
- Removed or moved dead/test-only production surface instead of suppressing it.
- Kept OS-specific build-tag files intact as valid platform boundaries.
- Fixed ClawSweeper finding: voice-note metadata probing now uses the real uploaded file path, not the optional display filename override.
- Fixed ClawSweeper finding: sent-file persistence now preserves the caller context when resolving chat names after send.
- Added focused regression coverage for the voice metadata path and sent-file context preservation fixes.

## Potential remaining risks

- This is still a broad refactor: 67 files changed across CLI, app, store, and WhatsApp integration code.
- Static analysis and tests are green, but command compatibility should still be reviewed carefully for send, sync, backfill, media, poll, status, and store paths.
- Live smoke proof currently covers text send/sync against Dovocoder / Assistent; it does not yet prove every file, voice, status, channel, and group send path against a live WhatsApp account.
- The two strict-mode informational build-tag notices remain by design and should stay unless CI/platform support changes.
- Store migration behavior should receive maintainer attention because schema and persistence paths are high-blast-radius even when tests pass.

## Why this is higher quality than main

This is not just scanner appeasement. The branch improves the codebase in ways
that should hold up during normal maintenance:

- removes the critical SQL-construction finding present on `main`
- breaks up large command/app functions into smaller helpers with clearer
  responsibilities
- reduces duplicated mutex/client, send, sync, message, and store patterns
- narrows internal API surface by unexporting symbols that do not need to be
  public inside their packages
- removes or moves dead/test-only production surface instead of suppressing it
- keeps the default analyzer gate at zero without `//gollaw:keep`, ignores, or
  relaxed yaml policy

My judgment: the branch is materially higher quality than `main`, especially for
maintainability and security posture. The caveat is that this is a broad
refactor across CLI, app, store, and WhatsApp integration paths, so it still
deserves careful review and smoke testing even though the static gate and tests
are green.

## wacli changes

- Refactored large Cobra command constructors and command `RunE` bodies into
  focused option structs and `run*` helpers.
- Reduced duplicated send/select/status/sticker/file command plumbing.
- Extracted repeated sync, backfill, message-store, poll, status, media, and WA
  client logic into smaller helpers.
- Tightened unexported/internal types and helper names where they were only used
  inside one package.
- Kept OS-specific build-tag files intact as valid platform boundaries.
- Avoided suppressions and broad configuration softening.

## gollaw-side improvements used by this branch

The current result depends on the stricter gollaw work that was developed along
the way:

- dead-code analysis now tracks main/init roots, generated migration-style
  registries, cobra command registration, and common Go call/reference shapes
  more accurately
- security analysis gives agent-fixable messages and flags real dynamic SQL
  construction instead of benign error/log formatting
- thin-wrapper, duplicate-code, large-function, API-surface, unused-member, and
  feature-flag checks were tightened so they are stricter where it matters and
  less noisy where Go/framework patterns are intentional

## Verification

Local verification on this branch:

- `/tmp/gollaw analyze . --format compact --no-suppress`
  - `TOTAL: 0 findings (0 critical, 0 warning, 0 info, 0 hint)`
- `/tmp/gollaw analyze . --format compact --min-severity hint --no-suppress`
  - `TOTAL: 2 findings (0 critical, 0 warning, 2 info, 0 hint)`
- `go test ./cmd/wacli`
- `go test ./...`
- `pnpm format:check`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm build`
- `git diff --check`

Main comparison from a clean worktree at `834c03f`:

- default gollaw: `24 findings (1 critical, 23 warning)`
- strict hint scan: `113 findings (1 critical, 23 warning, 4 info, 85 hint)`
- `go test ./...` also passes on main, so the difference is static
  quality/security/code-health findings rather than basic test pass/fail status.

Live WhatsApp smoke test against Dovocoder / Assistent:

- sent a text message to `Assistent`
- send returned success with message id `3EB0A09830F04596A2CC3C`
- `sync --once --idle-exit 20s` connected and exited cleanly
- local message listing showed the sent probe and an `OK` reply from Assistent

## Review risk

The result is cleaner than `main`, but the diff is broad: 67 files changed across
CLI, app, store, and WA integration code. Review should focus on behavioral
compatibility for command flags, sync/backfill paths, store migrations, and WA
send/media paths.
